In Bangladesh public procurement, under the Electronic Standard Tender Documents (eSTDs) on e-GP and the Public Procurement Rules, **NCT** (National Competitive Tendering) and **ICT** (International Competitive Tendering) are the two main methods for inviting bids. The choice depends on the geographic scope, value and technical complexity of the contract.

::: {.callout-warning}
Here **ICT** means *International* Competitive Tendering. It is unrelated to the ICT Division (Information and Communication Technology), which is mentioned further down as a place to find tech tenders.
:::

### Key Differences

| Feature | NCT (National) | ICT (International) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Participant scope** | Local suppliers, contractors or consultants within Bangladesh | Global and domestic suppliers and contractors |
| **Bidding language** | Typically the local language (Bangla) | English (and/or the local language) |
| **Market competition** | Domestic market only | International market |
| **Timeline** | Shorter bidding and processing windows | Longer, because of international advertising, shipping and clarification rules |
| **Bidder cost and complexity** | Lower cost, low regulatory complexity | Higher cost and complexity: foreign exchange, international law, multi-currency terms |
| **Typical use** | Routine goods, small-to-medium works, local services | Specialised goods, high-value contracts, technology-intensive or large infrastructure projects |

### Where to Find and Manage Tenders

- **e-GP portal:** the official electronic government procurement platform, where both NCT and ICT packages are published.
- **Line ministries and departments:** bodies such as the [ICT Division](https://ictd.gov.bd/pages/tenders) and the [Department of ICT](https://doict.gov.bd/pages/tenders) regularly post e-tender notices for technology tools, network installation and consultancy.
- **Aggregators:** sites like [BDTender](https://bdtender.com/dept/Org-673/ministry-information-communication-technology/ict-division-tender-notice) collect active notices from the ICT ministry and related sectors.

### Choosing Between Them

Start with who can realistically supply the item. If the local market can deliver at fair value, NCT is faster and cheaper for everyone. If the item is specialised or high-value enough that foreign suppliers are needed for real competition, ICT is the route, at the price of a longer timeline and heavier bidder paperwork.
